en.title: Minimum Increase for the Most Strict Peaks
en.description:
You may only increase array elements, and each increment is an integer in 0..10^18. An interior point counts as a peak only if it is strictly greater than both neighbors; endpoints do not count. First maximize the number of peaks, then minimize the total increase.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and the solution; supplements for missing source bounds and example corrections are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n initial values. The original gives no bounds on n or the initial values; this site uses 1≤n≤200000 with initial values in −10^9..10^9, and keeps the original upper limit of 10^18 per increment.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1; 10; 0. Checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Compute the cost of making each interior point a peak on its own. For odd lengths, only odd indices can be chosen; for even lengths, enumerate the switch point where a run of odd indices is followed by a run of even indices.
